NEXT SUNDAY: ROAD CLOSURES
FOR CARDIFF HALF MARATHON


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Road closures will affect our community on the morning of Sunday 4th October for the Cardiff Half Marathon.

Penarth Road, Barry Road and Cogan Spur will all be closed, as the marathon course runs along these roads.

Llandough Hill will also be closed, to prevent vehicles diverted via Penlan Road from inadvertently trying to access Penarth Road while it's shut.
Diversions will be in place, and you can see the full road closure map above.

The closures will operate between 9am and 12pm.

Further details can be found at the Cardiff Half Marathon website here.  (https://www.cardiffhalfmarathon.co.uk/event-info/road-closures/)

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1BzkRccTvm/

If you have further questions, Requester, please let me know.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

Next community litter pick

Our last community litter pick has had great feedback.

I've even had a couple of messages asking when the next one is taking place!

Llandough Community Council organise these events throughout the year, but they usually put them on hold during the winter, due to lack of interest.

But given the enthusiasm, I thought it best to harness it!

We discussed it at last week's Community Council meeting, and I'm exploring organising another in the coming weeks.

I'll need to liaise with the Vale Council to arrange equipment, but the Community Council are on board and have said they'll help.

If you're interested in taking part, Requester, drop me a message!
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1KDWx1SUjX/

Licensing Service of
Revd Phil Maudsley

I had a wonderful evening on Tuesday at the Licensing Service of Reverend Phil Maudsley, the new Penarth Ministry Area lead.

It was great to see many members of our community there, including Llandough Community Council Chair Mo Misra, Reverend Susannah Griffin and lots of other residents.

Phil and his family have recently moved to South Wales from North Yorkshire, and I look forward to working with him.

I know everyone in Llandough will join me in welcoming them to our community.

Greenway Close verge

When I was out in our village recently, a Greenway Close resident raised the overgrowth on the nearby verge.

As you'll see from the first picture, it was in need of attention.

I raised with the Council. And I'm pleased to report it's now been cut back.

Thanks so much to the resident for coming over and raising this.

It helped ensure it was cleared.

As I always say, we're a team in Llandough.

By all chipping in, we make our village better for everyone.

If you ever spot anything that needs attention, Requester, do let me know!

Preventing car thefts

I spoke with two people who've recently purchased Faraday boxes while I was out meeting residents this week.

With attempted car thefts reported in our village in recent months, police have advised everyone with keyless fobs to keep them in a Faraday pouch or box as a security measure.

It's a sensible precaution and a small expense to protect your car.

It was good to see people following the advice.

If you require further information, please drop me a message.

Community drop-in event:
20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

Like the last one, it'll start at 7.00pm.

The pub is a key asset to our community.

Tracey and the team do a lot for us - help return the favour by lending them your support.

You can see some of their midweek offers below!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EM9z5wbMs/

Our Plan for Llandough!


As your councillor, I'm working with you all to secure a better future for Llandough. Together, we have a plan to deliver for the village.

Our plan is making Llandough better by:

1. Sorting out the parking problems
2. Stamping out dog fouling
3. Repairing our roads
4. Stopping littering and flytipping
5. Delivering better sports facilities
6. Keeping the whole community involved

If you have any suggestions of what you'd like to see in Our Plan, please get in touch!

Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-032

Diolch yn fawr. Thank you for the records, the descriptors and the published references. This is a thorough response and it is genuinely useful.

One correction of place is required.

The request concerns Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough near Penarth / Cardiff. Among the disclosed PAS material is at least one record for a different property of the same name: Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge (including 2022.18.1, NGR SS9934672805, medieval lead Romanesque mount). There is also a Great House farm entry at Llandow. Those are not the site named in the request. Two Llandoughs, and more than one Great House Farm, sit in the same county. The homonym is easy to miss and material.

Please treat the Cowbridge / Llandow entries as out of scope for this request unless you hold recorded information showing they were, at any time, indexed, cited, or treated as if they related to Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Cardiff). If any such cross-attribution exists in historic files, catalogues, correspondence, or search notes, that recorded information is within scope and I ask that it be disclosed.

If labels or findspot fields are now amended to distinguish the two farms, please do not overwrite the original wording without retaining the prior form. I ask that any correction be recorded as a dated amendment, with the earlier descriptor preserved, so the sequence of how the records stood when searches were first run remains inspectable. Please do not destroy, weed, or replace the versions as disclosed on 22 September 2026.

One small point from my email of 26 August also remains. As item 7 I asked for any recorded information showing the basis on which the Museum concluded that the identified records were unrelated to the reported nineteenth-century discovery. If that conclusion was reached by staff judgement and not written down, please simply confirm that no recorded information is held on that point. I am not asking for a new opinion.

Could you also confirm the date by which you expect to respond to FOI 2026-036?

Cofion,

Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Requester,

Your email of the 21st September has been passed over to our clerk (in 
copy) for consideration.

Best regards

---
Dr Mo Misra, Chair Llandough Community Council

On 2026-09-21 03:59, Requester wrote:

> Dr Misra,
> 
> Thank you for replying, and for doing so promptly and at a weekend. 
> Good drills Sir. What an honour. I know you and the Council serve as 
> volunteers, and I am grateful for the time.
> 
> Let me set out plainly what I am asking of the Council, which is 
> narrow. If you'll allow me?
> 
> I am not asking your Council to revisit Mr Egan's answer of 14 June 
> 2026. He explained that the minute books from 1982 onwards were 
> deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002, and I am pursuing those 
> there.
> 
> What I am asking about is what that answer did not cover. Llandough 
> Community Council is a public authority under Schedule 1, Part II, 
> paragraph 7(b) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000. The Act applies 
> to the recorded information set out below generally; the Environmental 
> Information Regulations 2004 apply in addition to any part of it that 
> is environmental information.
> 
> PART ONE -- REQUEST FOR RECORDED INFORMATION
> 
> 1. Whether the Council holds any recorded information created after the 
> 2002 deposit -- minutes, correspondence, reports, emails, photographs 
> or files of any kind -- concerning Great House Farm (Ty Mawr) / Church 
> View Close, the village green in front of St Dochdwy's including 
> registered green VG 41, or the roadside verge by the churchyard wall.
> 
> 2. Whether the Council holds any photographs, postcards or images of 
> the farm, the barn, the green or the church surroundings, of any date.
> 
> 3. Whether the Council holds any recorded information showing what, if 
> anything, transferred to it from Penarth Town Council at the 1982 
> reorganisation, and any recorded information identifying where the 
> pre-1982 Llandough community records were deposited.
> 
> If the answer to any of these is that no such information is held, I 
> would be content with a short statement to that effect -- but I do need 
> it stated. Section 1(1)(a) of the Act requires the Council to confirm 
> or deny whether the information is held.
> 
> Section 10 (and regulation 5 of the EIR) allows twenty working days 
> from receipt, which on my request of 20 September 2026 I calculate as 
> 16 October 2026.
> 
> If the Council is refusing, section 17 (and regulation 14) requires a 
> written refusal notice identifying the exemption or exception relied 
> on; section 17(7) requires the Council to give particulars of any 
> complaints procedure it operates, or to state that it has none, and to 
> notify me of my right to apply to the Information Commissioner; and 
> regulation 11 gives a right to an internal review of any refusal under 
> the EIR.
> 
> "We have nothing more to add" does not meet those requirements. If the 
> period passes without a compliant response I will have no option but to 
> complain to the Information Commissioner.
> 
> PART TWO -- MATTERS FOR THE COUNCIL'S DISCRETION
> 
> These are not part of the request above and carry no deadline. They are 
> simply things I would be grateful for.
> 
> A. I am not asking for the name or contact details of any individual. I 
> am asking whether the Council would be willing to pass my details to 
> any former member, former clerk or long-standing resident who might 
> remember the village between the 1950s and the 1990s, leaving it 
> entirely to them whether to contact me. I appreciate the Council may 
> have data protection or administrative reasons for declining, and I 
> would not press it.
> 
> B. Whether the Council would be willing to table this correspondence at 
> a meeting and minute it. I am content for it to be tabled in full.
> 
> C. Whether the Council would consider, in due course, whether an 
> interpretation board or a plaque near the green would be appropriate. 
> The excavation on the land beneath Church View Close recorded 1,026 
> burials, described in the published report as by far the largest early 
> medieval burial population so far recovered from Wales, above a Roman 
> villa and an Iron Age roundhouse. That history belongs to Llandough as 
> much as to my family, and there is nothing on the ground that records 
> it. I would be glad to give the Council or the community a short talk 
> on the documentary record, without charge, if that would be useful.
> 
> I should be grateful for a response to items 1 to 3 by 16 October 2026.
> 
> Regards,
> 
> Requester 
> 
> 
> On Sun, 20 Sept 2026, 18:31 Mo Misra, <[email redacted]> 
> wrote:
> 
>> Dear Requester,
>> 
>> Thanks for your email of 20th September 2026.
>> 
>> I note that our Clerk, Paul Egan, has already directed you to all the
>> information we have on the matter as indicated in paragraph 6 of your
>> email.
>> 
>> We have nothing more to add.
>> 
>> Best regards
>>

*FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE*
*Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth*
*Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527*
*Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES*

*URL: **greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
 *

*To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or
potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:*

This notice is addressed to each recipient *individually*. It is *not a
joint request*, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate
on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each
recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that
recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited
from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.
1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a *formal preservation notice* concerning documentary material
relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining
St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the
area now associated with Church View Close.

It is *not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended
to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint,
subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any
recipient.*

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially
relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration
history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and
subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being
issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and
DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO,
Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the
Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes
(Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

*You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary
record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your
custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional,
administrative or development chain concerning this land.*
2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer
out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any
record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or
matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, *originals, copies, working papers,
drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps,
registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic
files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting
records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other
associated records.*

The material requested includes:

*1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing*

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western
Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust
conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence
or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

*2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation*

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the
1974 proceedings; *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2*; House of
Lords leave papers, including *YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536*; and *Buckler v United
Kingdom (1989)*, including associated correspondence, instructions,
evidence, plans and working papers.

*3. Land registration*

The first registration of *WA231076*, including the application dated 30
November 1982; the first registration of *WA240304*, including the
application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or
closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application,
correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with
those registrations or changes.

*4. 1988 possession and demolition*

The taking of possession on or about *29 November 1988* and the demolition
commenced on or about *6 December 1988*, including any planning,
listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey,
photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

*5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996*

Planning application *89/01396/OUT*; reserved matters application
*92/00671/RES*; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material;
records concerning any *section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local
land charge or equivalent instrument*; and the transfer from BP to Ideal
Homes dated *3 December 1993*, together with all associated plans,
correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

*6. Family records*

Records concerning *Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983)* and *William Buckler*,
insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land
described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal,
registration, development or demolition.
3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor,
successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity,
that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

*Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan;
Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn
Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust;
Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and
South Glamorgan County Council.*

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily
hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or
succession inquiry should be made where applicable.
4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion,
alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including
material held in *archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage,
document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or
physical stores*.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository,
archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the
information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location,
including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist.
The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled
by you.
5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is *not a finding against any recipient*, and I am not asking
any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The *1987 Court of Appeal judgment* is relied upon here only for matters
actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning
possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation
notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete
documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the
farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through
Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from
the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary
record can be established from the records themselves rather than through
assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning
treatment or secondary descriptions.
6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity,
confirm:

*(a)* the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for
implementing the preservation hold;

*(b)* what records within your possession, custody or control you have
identified as falling within the scope above; and

*(c)* where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems,
files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that
conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate
requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material
you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

*https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
 *

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents,
references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation
notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to
*Loosemores,
Alliance House, 18–19 High Street, Cardiff [postcode redacted]*.

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of
any claim, position or remedy concerning *title, registration, concealment,
limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any
associated matter.*

Regards,

*Requester *

records.transcript:
Information Governance Team
Vale of Glamorgan Council
[email redacted]
cc: [email redacted]

Sirs/Madam,

New request under FOIA 2000 and/or EIR 2004. Do not treat this as a reopening or expansion of 00210772, 00211463 or 00211484. Those cases stay as they are.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Leckwith Road, Llandough, later Church View Close.
Applications: 89/01396/OUT (outline granted 13 March 1990) and 92/00671/RES.

I already have, or have already asked for, the officer's report, Policy H.2 text, Appendices C–E, the decision notices, and the general archaeological-condition papers. This request is confined to classes that those earlier requests did not name.

Please disclose recorded information held, or confirm item by item if not held:

1. Section 52 / later section 106 / land charges
Any agreement under section 52 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1971, any later section 106 instrument, any deed, undertaking or other agreement regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding entry on the local land charges register. Search legal, planning and land-charges holdings, not only the 2026 planning-file scan. If none is held, say so expressly. That is an open records question, not a conclusion that none existed.

2. Historic planning register
The planning-register entries that the Town and Country Planning General Development Order 1988 required the authority to keep for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES: the applications, reserved-matters applications, plans and drawings, and relevant decision information. If the 2026 file disclosure is incomplete against that register, say what the register still lists and what is missing from the file.

3. Appendix B
Appendix B to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT: the further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust. Case 00211463 asked for C, D and E and for a list of annexes. It did not ask for B by that description. If B is not held, say when it left the file, under what retention rule, and whether any copy survives elsewhere.

4. Condition 16–18 chain
Named papers, not a general search:
(a) conditions 16, 17 and 18 as issued on the 13 March 1990 permission;
(b) the Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17;
(c) GGAT's archaeological warning of July 1992;
(d) the September 1992 reserved-matters approval, and whether any further archaeological condition was attached;
(e) the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters recommending a breach-of-condition notice.

5. Environmental assessment / screening
Any preliminary environmental-assessment determination, screening opinion, or recorded decision that an environmental statement was or was not required for 89/01396/OUT. The application site is described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38 hectares. I am not asserting that an environmental statement was required. I am asking whether the Council made and recorded the determination at all.

6. Archaeological-interest consultation route
Any record of the statutory consultation route actually used because the land was recorded in the county Sites and Monuments Record, or was treated as a "site of archaeological interest" under the 1988 Order. I am not asking you to treat SMR status as automatic proof of a particular duty. I am asking what route was used.

7. Application receipt date
The Council's receipt record for 89/01396/OUT. The application form is dated October 1989. The reconstructed planning record gives 8 November 1989 as receipt of the application and plans. Please supply the date-stamped receipt, validation or register entry.

8. 92/00671/RES completeness and applicant standing
(a) A file list or register for 92/00671/RES showing what the reserved-matters file originally contained.
(b) Any sale, option, conditional-contract or authority-to-apply paper on the planning files covering the change from BP Properties (1989 outline applicant) to Ideal Homes Wales (appearing on the 1992 reserved-matters trail), including the recorded BP-to-Ideal Homes transfer of 3 December 1993.
This is a documentary interest/authority question. It is not an allegation that the 1992 application was invalid.

If a record is not held, say so for that item. If it was destroyed, transferred or archived, give the date, the schedule, and any surviving catalogue. Search planning, legal, land charges and archived/scanned holdings.

Please give a new reference and the 20 working-day date. Preserve anything in scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . I am not asking the Council to decide title.

Yours faithfully,

Requester 
[email redacted]

I am not asking you to adopt a legal conclusion. I am asking you to look at a primary record that is now public, before more of it is lost.

What the record shows, as distinct from what is still a question:

Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr stood by St Dochdwy's, Llandough. Possession was taken on 29 November 1988. Demolition of the farmhouse began on 6 December 1988. The land is now Church View Close. The current registered proprietor of WA231076 is Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd. First-registration applications were made on 30 November 1982 (WA231076) and 23 February 1983 (WA240304, later closed into WA231076).

The family's investigation is that the house and garden were a separate parcel from the eastern fields, and that later papers used "whole farm" for both. A Vale of Glamorgan internal review requested on 7 July (00210772) has no outcome. HM Land Registry file N610CGV is with the Independent Complaints Reviewer. A replica of the house is being built in the Welsh settlement in Patagonia as a museum, not as restitution.

Annwyl Requester,

Diolch yn fawr am eich ymholiadau o 8, 15, 17 ac 20 Medi. Fel y awgrymir yn eich e-bost o 20 Medi, gwnaf ateb eich ymholiadau gyda’i gilydd.

Nid oes unrhyw gofnodion wedi dod i’r amlwg yn ystod y cyfnod ers hynny. Yn sgil hynny, yr unig wybodaeth sydd gennem ynglŷn â’r safle, gan gynnwys ei dymchwel, yw’r cofnodion yn ein harchif, sef Cofnod Henebion Cenedlaethol Cymru. Gellir gweld rhestr lawn ohonynt yma: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/sites/20182/archives. Ynglŷn ag awyrluniau, oherwydd cymhlethdod y casgliad hwn, byddai rhaid talu ar gyfer y chwiliadau hyn (gwelir y rhestr brisiau, a atodir, ar gyfer manylion). Petasai awyrluniau sydd yn cynnwys y safle yn bodoli, y mae’n debygol y byddent yn awyrluniau fertigol wedi’u tynnu o uchder uchel fel rhan o waith arolwg y tirlun arferol ac nid fyddent yn canolbwyntio ar y safle, na ei ddangos yn fanwl.

Ynglŷn â’ch ymholiad ynglŷn â’r arwisg a darganfuwyd yn ystod y bedwaredd ganrif ar bymtheg hwyr, nid oes sylw arno yn yr adroddiad gan Richard Suggett heb ei chyhoeddi, sef Rhif Archif 6048945 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048945). Gyda llaw, mae rhan fwyaf o’r cofnod hon wedi’i thanysgrifennu fel disgrifiad y safle gan Heneb, GGAT02038s (https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core&sessid=CHI4nj4fn3q&queryid=Q383581001790598378). Yr wyf yn gynnwys eu disgrifiad isod, wedi’i gwirio er mwyn adlewyrchu y testun gwreiddiol:
‘Great House Farmhouse and barn formed an attractive group, built of local lias limestone, and occupied an historic site next to the parish church. Finds of medieval ironwork and pottery have been reported from the site. Great House was the chief freehold farm of the parish and was occupied by the Vaughan's, a minor gentry family, from the mid C16 until the latter part of the C18. Several memorial inscriptions relating to the family are preserved in the church and churchyard. In the early C19 the freehold was acquired by the Bute Estate and the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith were held in Great House.

‘Externally both farmhouse and barn appeared to be of nineteenth-century date. Internally, however, surviving vernacular detail- a blocked stone fireplace stair and agee-stopped beams- suggested a seventeenth-century date for the house. The ground floor of the house was surveyed in unusual circumstances in 1974 by H.J.T. Much detail was then concealed and it was not possible to examine the first floor and roof trusses. The house remained partially recorded because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute. The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy.

‘The plan of Great House was not published in the Inventory of Farmhouses & Cottages because of the incompleteness of the available information but it was classified as a sub-medieval house of direct-entry type (site no. 425). However, certain features suggested that the core of the house may have been medieval. The clearly-defined cross-passage end-chimney plan with masonry partitions and external wall batter (on the unreconstructed N side) had clear affinities with Brynwell, a medieval farmhouse in the neighbouring parish of Leckwith, Brynwell was built as a direct-entry, end-chimney, storeyed pre-Reformation house (Inventory, pp.187, 192). Brynwell, like Great House, was modernised in the C19th by the Bute Estate but the medieval date of the house is clearly shown by a small first-floor cusped-head window and the remodelled roof trusses. Unfortunately it was not possible to examine the fabric of Great House before the demolition of the house. Examination of the rubble brought to light no new features except an ogee-stopped beam with torus, a form of decoration that is not particularly common in Glamorgan (Inventory, Map 50).’

Er hynny, y mae dau gofnod sydd yn cyfeirio at ddarganfod yr arwisg, sef Rhif Archif 6048942 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048942), le y nodir ‘At one time it was reputed to be the stable of a Castle, which could be verified by the finding of the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, lance and small shield under the dining room floor’, a Rhif Archif 6048944 (https://coflein.gov.uk/en/archives/6048944), sef erthygl o’r Daily Telegraph, 16 Ebrill 1974, le y nodir ‘Its history has never been fully chronicled but a theory that it was originally a coaching house near a Castle was supported by the discovery benieth the dining room floor in about 1870 of the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, a lance and shield’. From: Requester  
Sent: 22 September 2026 16:51
To: Wigley, Andy (LCC - Cadw)  
Cc: Complaints - Cwynion  ; Cadw Planning  
Subject: Supplement to complaint re-served 20 September 2026 — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough

Dr Wigley,

This is a supplement to the complaint re-served on 20 September, not a chaser. I do not expect a reply before the stage-one response. It adds seven matters under the existing headings at section 7, and one addition to the outcomes at section 9, set out at the end.

The public interest is engaged alongside my family's. Great House Farm stood beside the Grade I church at Llandough, was recorded by the Royal Commission in 1974, sat within a known archaeological site, and was described in the post-demolition planning record as a "county treasure". I do not ask Cadw to treat the 1994 discoveries as knowledge it had in 1988. They show what was lost; the pre-1988 record is the measure of Cadw's process.

On my family's account and the contemporary press report, protection was being sought in the first days of December 1988 and the house was demolished almost immediately afterwards. I do not ask Cadw to determine responsibility for the demolition. The grievance is narrower: protection was sought at the critical moment, and Cadw cannot now show what it considered.

1. The adopted development plan (matter A)

The planning officer's report on application 89/01396/OUT records that the supporting information to Policy H.2 of the East Vale Local Plan "states that buildings on the site should be retained, however were unfortunately demolished a little while ago." I do not say this bound Cadw or required listing. I ask:
(a) was Cadw aware of it in December 1988;
(b) did the planning authority draw it to Cadw's attention; and
(c) if neither can be established, will Cadw say so expressly.

2. The search undertaken on 21 May (matters D and F)

Mr Weatherhead wrote that he had asked a colleague to search other paper files, "including the Welsh Office files", and would write again with the result, while fairly warning that some files had quite likely been destroyed. I have not received that letter. Please confirm whether the search was carried out, which series were searched, what was found, and whether Cadw regards the ATISN 27021 response of 11 June as its report of that search.

3. The meaning of "YYY" (matter J)

Cadw has given two accounts of the marking — that the buildings were "marginally below the bar for listing" (21 May) and that the building did not meet the criteria (10 July) — and one inference, that it did not meet the criteria "as it was not included on the list" (29 July). I ask for one settled meaning, the documentary source for it, and, if there is none, a statement to that effect.

4. The retention period (matter J)

Your email of 27 August said that no records of the historic retention arrangements are available, and that the three-year period is what current colleagues advised from their knowledge of the systems then in place. I ask only that the complaint response confirm expressly that this is an account of general practice, not evidence that the Great House Farm file was in fact destroyed after three years.

5. Professional archaeological knowledge of this site before December 1988 (matter C)

On 22 September 2026 Amgueddfa Cymru disclosed to me, under FOI 2026-032, its collections records for two accessions from this site. The first, 82.44H, is the material from the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust's excavation of 1979 on land formerly part of Great House Farm, carried out in advance of housing development. The museum's records give the findspot as ST 168 733, the donor as Wales & West Housing Association Ltd, and the published report as Owen-John 1988. The accession runs to several hundred entries and includes Roman coins, samian, glass, a bone scabbard slide and querns, together with medieval pottery and ironwork.

This is not archaeology discovered after the event. By the time Cadw considered this building, the site had been professionally excavated, the finds had been accessioned by the national museum under a 1982 accession number, and the excavation report had been published. I therefore ask, as an addition to matter C:
(a) whether Cadw held, or had access to, the 1979 excavation record or its published report when it considered the buildings in 1988;
(b) whether that material was drawn to its attention by GGAT, the planning authority or the Royal Commission; and
(c) if neither can now be established, that Cadw say so in terms.

I do not say this material required the building to be listed. I say that the conclusion recorded in December 1988, that the site was not of sufficient archaeological interest, was reached against a professional record that already existed and is still held by the national museum today.

6. The National Museum attribution (matter H)

The GGAT assessment of August 1990, which Cadw supplied to me on 21 May, states that "it is likely that some medieval ironwork which is held by the National Museum of Wales was discovered under the rear wing c 1880 (RCAHMW 1988)."

The museum's disclosure allows that sentence to be tested, and the position is more precise than either of us has previously put it. The museum does hold medieval ironwork from this site — knife blades, arrowheads, a buckle and a pair of compasses within accession 82.44H — but as excavated material from 1979, not as an 1880 discovery beneath the rear wing. Its searches found no accession, donation or deposit answering the c.1880 provenance at all. The museum's own explanation, given in its disclosure, is that objects recorded as found at Church Farm, Llandough in 1858 and donated in 1963 under accession 63.24 "could well be the basis for such a local story/tradition".

I therefore no longer ask Cadw to accept that the attribution is uncorroborated in the round. I ask, more narrowly, whether Cadw holds anything supporting the c.1880 rear-wing provenance beyond the GGAT sentence it forwarded, and whether it will ask that the derived record note the museum's findings rather than continue to carry the 1880 attribution unqualified.

7. Correcting the record (matter H)

You directed me to Heneb as manager of the HER, which was reasonable. The only substantive reply I have had from Heneb is its statement of 22 May that it is not subject to FOI as a limited company; a schedule I sent on 19 September remains outstanding.

The museum's disclosure now gives a firm anchor for what the record should show. Accession 95.56H comprises the material from the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavation of 1994, donated by Ideal Homes Wales Ltd, and its locality is recorded in the museum's own collections database as "Great House Farm Llandough" at ST 1681 7331 — the grid reference carried by the historic environment record for this site. That accession runs to several hundred sets of early medieval human remains from this ground.

As the statutory duty to keep historic environment records rests with the Welsh Ministers, I ask:
(a) which body is responsible for correcting an inaccurate or incomplete historic environment record;
(b) what Cadw's own role is where the record is managed by Heneb; and
(c) what Cadw will do if the entry for this site (GGAT02038s) is not corrected to reflect the 1979 and 1994 excavations and the accessions arising from them.

Correction to my letter of 20 September

I said [email redacted]  had rejected my correspondence on three occasions. Having checked properly, it rejected messages on at least eight occasions between January and September 2026: 23 January; 9 May (twice); 17 May; 10 August; 11 August; 29 August; and 17 September. Separate failures on 29 August and 17 September came from the retired address [email redacted] . I correct this because I have asked Cadw to distinguish what is established from what is inferred, and the same standard applies to me.

Addition to the outcomes at section 9

6. A written acknowledgement that the 21 May undertaking was not reported on, and that Cadw's accounts of the 1988 assessment have varied.
7. A single statement of what can and cannot now be established about the 1988 decisions, which my family can rely on and cite.
8. That Cadw write to Heneb and the Royal Commission asking that their records for this site reflect that statement and the museum's accession records.
9. Consideration, under the Welsh Government complaints policy, of redress for the time and trouble my family has spent since May pursuing questions that Cadw's own records could not answer.

I am content to supply the museum's disclosure to Cadw if that would assist, and my offer of 20 September stands: any 1988 Cadw correspondence recovered from the Royal Commission or Heneb will be sent to you. I remain grateful for the courtesy you and your colleagues have shown me.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Preservation notice — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — do not destroy, transfer or dispose
To each recipient, in your own capacity as holder or likely holder of
records. Please do not treat this as a joint reply. Answer only for
your own holdings.

Sirs/Madam,

This is a preservation notice. It is not a claim form and not service
of proceedings. It does not replace any FOI, review or subject access
request already with you.

Land: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining
St Dochdwy's. Titles WA231076, WA240304 (closed), WA513690, WA735527,
and any related title. Planning refs 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES.

Please preserve, and do not destroy, transfer out of your custody
without a written receipt, or dispose of, any file, plan, photograph,
tape or electronic record in your possession, custody or control
relating to:

1. The 1877 split, the 1916 and 1939 tenancies, and the 1938 Bute to
Western Ground Rents conveyance.
2. The 1955 and 1962 possession orders, the 1974 proceedings, and BP
Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2.
3. First registration: WA231076 application 30 November 1982; WA240304
application 23 February 1983; later amalgamation.
4. The 1988 possession (29 November) and demolition (begun 6
December), including listing, planning, police and any liaison papers.
5. Mary Doreen Williams (died 26 March 1983) and William Buckler, so
far as your file concerns this land.

Also preserve, if you hold them, the following planning and
land-charge classes. Absence from a 2026 file disclosure is not proof
they never existed:

6. Any section 52 Town and Country Planning Act 1971 agreement, later
section 106 instrument, deed, undertaking or other agreement
regulating the development or use of this land, and any corresponding
local-land-charge entry.
7. The historic planning-register entries required by the Town and
Country Planning General Development Order 1988 for 89/01396/OUT and
92/00671/RES (applications, reserved matters, plans and drawings, and
decision information).
8. The officer's report annexes to 89/01396/OUT, including Appendix B
(further GGAT comments after discussions with the Trust), and
Appendices C–E.
9. The condition chain on 89/01396/OUT: conditions 16–18; the
Council's October 1990 confirmation of condition 17; GGAT's July 1992
archaeological warning; the September 1992 reserved-matters approval;
and the 1993–94 papers on whether condition 18 had been discharged.
10. Any preliminary environmental-assessment / screening determination
for the outline application (site described as about 3.4 acres / 1.38
ha).
11. Any record of the statutory consultation route used because the
land was, or was treated as, a site of archaeological interest / SMR
entry under the 1988 Order.
12. The complete 92/00671/RES file, and any sale, option,
conditional-contract or transfer paper on the planning files covering
BP Properties to Ideal Homes Wales, including the recorded transfer of
3 December 1993.
13. The application-receipt record for 89/01396/OUT (form dated
October 1989; reconstructed Council receipt 8 November 1989).

Please stop routine deletion, including archived mailboxes, for
anything in that scope.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
. The investigation distinguishes the farmhouse parcel from the
eastern fields. The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession,
limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the
documentary root of the farmhouse parcel. These records go to that
question. This notice is not a finding against any of you.

Please acknowledge, name the officer responsible for the hold, and say
what you hold in scope. If you hold nothing, say what you searched.

Nothing in this letter abandons any claim concerning title,
registration, concealment, limitation, reopening or alteration of the
register.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Louise,

I just want to clarify one important point in relation to my original enquiry, as I think I may have caused a slight misunderstanding about the particular transaction I am trying to establish.

My principal question is not whether there are deeds between the Bute Estate and Alfred Thomas.
